newsitem.title: UK: Short Bros says couldn't stay in limbo over Fokker.
newsitem.headline: Short Bros says couldn't stay in limbo over Fokker.

text.p: Northern Ireland's Short Brothers Plc, which effectively scuppered hopes for a rescue of Fokker on Thursday, said it had been unwilling to remain in limbo awaiting a decision on the Dutch planemaker's future.

The Belfast-based aerospace company, a subsidiary of Canada's Bombardier Inc, said it would no longer supply wings to Fokker, leading Fokker's administrators to say a relaunch of the company was no longer feasible.

Samsung Aerospace had been in talks to acquire Fokker, but said on Thursday it required another month to decide whether or not to take over the company. Shorts said it could no no longer accept the delays in a decision on Fokker's future.

"We had to be able to get on with our future," a spokesman for Shorts said. "Samsung seemed unable to reach a decision with its partners and the South Korean government and in the end suppliers like ourselves had to say enough is enough."

"We lost nearly 1000 jobs with the collapse of Fokker and our main factory has lain idle for nine months," he told Reuters. "We will now be able to get on with our future and install on our production lines new work that we are winning."

The spokesman said Shorts had told Fokker's administrators that although it was no longer willing to do the final assembly of wings for Fokker, it was still willing to help in "all other ways," such as offering technical expertise and aiding the transfer of production of the wings to another source.
"We very much regret that the trustees decided not to proceed with discussions to transfer production elsewhere," he said.
Shorts said it had already won new business since the collapse of Fokker and was in negotiations to secure more.

"Within three or four years we hope to have won enough business to replace the business lost over Fokker," the spokesman said. "In the last few months we have started to recruit people again, and prospects for the future are looking good."
